title: Transferring a KestrelCare Plan on a Private Sale of the Vehicle
content:
When the holder sells the vehicle privately, an active KestrelCare Vehicle Service Contracts plan may be transferred to the buyer when all of the following hold:

- the plan is transferable;
- the transfers so far are below the plan's maximum transfers;
- the buyer is not a dealer;
- the transfer is requested within the transfer request days after the vehicle sale.

The holder pays the plan's transfer fee. The plan keeps its expiration date, expiration odometer and coverage remaining. A plan that is not transferable can only be cancelled. A transfer fee is charged only on a plan whose status is transferred, as the service contract record shows it.

The transfer is the holder's own act: the holder transfers the plan to the private buyer of the vehicle, and the plan's status moves from active to transferred.

## Cases (hypothetical plans)

| Plan | Situation | Transfer |
|---|---|---|
| KestrelCare Silver, active, no transfers yet | private buyer, requested 12 days after the sale | may be transferred; the holder pays the KestrelCare Silver transfer fee |
| KestrelCare Gold, active, transferred once | private buyer | not transferred: transfers so far are not below the maximum of one |
| KestrelCare Platinum, active | the buyer is a used-car dealer | not transferred |
| KestrelCare Powertrain, active | private buyer | not transferable; the plan can only be cancelled |

A transferred plan with 9400.00 of coverage remaining and an expiration odometer of 95000 still shows 9400.00 and 95000 after the transfer.
